summary.oneLiner: Q4FY26 revenue dipped 1.6% YoY due to West Asia-driven supply chain disruptions causing shipment deferrals, while FY26 PAT fell 24.7% due to elevated fixed costs from new capacity; however, gross margins improved sequentially to 41.9% and a strategic pivot to domestic markets (17% mix) plus a new bamboo vertical provides clear recovery levers for FY27.

one-line thesis: Q4FY26 revenue dipped 1.6% YoY due to West Asia-driven supply chain disruptions causing shipment deferrals, while FY26 PAT fell 24.7% due to elevated fixed costs from new capacity; however, gross margins improved sequentially to 41.9% and a strategic pivot to domestic markets (17% mix) plus a new bamboo vertical provides clear recovery levers for FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 145.8cr (Q4, -1.6% YoY), INR 610.4cr (FY26, +9.4% YoY); EBITDA: INR 21.6cr (Q4, 14.8% margin), INR 90.1cr (FY26, 14.8% margin vs 16.5% prior); PAT: INR 9.4cr (Q4), INR 35.6cr (FY26, -24.7% YoY) - distorted by INR 29cr depreciation (up from 23.5cr) and employee cost hikes; Order Book: Decent, no cancellations only deferrals; Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but operating cash flow doubled to INR 86.3cr.
guidance: Revenue growth: Targeting 70-75% capacity utilization in FY27 (up from 73% weighted avg in FY26); Margin: Expect EBITDA margin recovery to historical levels (18-19%) in H2FY27 as fixed costs absorb; Order inflow: Stable, deferred Q4 volumes (~10-15%) moving to Q1; Capex: INR 15cr for bamboo unit commissioning in H2FY27.
order book & pipeline: No cancellations reported; ~10-15% of Q4 volumes (approx. INR 3-5cr) deferred to Q1FY27 due to port congestion and raw material delays; Customers rolling out forecasts despite price hikes.
segment / subsidiary detail: Exports: 83% of revenue (Europe 58%, UK 12%, US 12%); Domestic: 17% (All-Time branded 15%, White label 2%); IKEA contribution: 55% in Q4 (vs 57% prior); Third largest customer grew 225%.
growth verticals / optionality: Bamboo board unit (3,000 cubic meters capacity) to start revenue contribution in H2FY27 with potential INR 60cr revenue at full utilization; Domestic B2C target raised to 22-25% mix over next 12-18 months.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded to 41.9% in Q4 (vs 39.1% YoY) due to product mix; EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% due to higher depreciation (INR 29cr) and employee/contract labor costs; Raw material prices down 10-15% from peaks but only 10-12% pass-through accepted by customers temporarily.
capex / expansion: Khatalwada expansion completed (total plastic capacity 39,000 MT, rising to 41,000 MT shortly); Bamboo facility lease signed (Guwahati), machinery ordered, INR 15cr investment; Remaining 6,000 MT plastic expansion paused pending demand clarity.
capital allocation: Focus on completing bamboo commissioning and organic capacity ramp; Operating cash flow of INR 86.3cr supports working capital and modest capex; No M&A mentioned.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension affecting raw material logistics; Inability to fully pass through 22-25% raw material price hikes (customers accepting only 10-12%); Delay in bamboo commercialization; Customer concentration (IKEA 55%).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges short-term headwinds (Q4 disruptions, margin pressure) but emphasizes structural growth, improved gross margins, and strong cash flows as foundations for FY27 recovery.
non-obvious takeaways: Recycled polymer volume grew 12.4% YoY to 8,022 MT, signaling sustainability push; 8-week lag in price pass-through for largest customer creates temporary margin gap; 90% of exports are FOB, mitigating freight risk despite port congestion.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility and supply chain disruptions hurting margins temporarily | Supreme Industries | beneficiary | Med | Larger peer with diversified portfolio may gain share if smaller exporters struggle with working capital during price hikes |
| Shift to sustainable alternatives and regulatory push for non-plastic materials | Greenpanel Industries | beneficiary | Low | Bamboo entry by All Time validates the segment but Greenpanel remains the pure-play leader |

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
